Chapter 9: Born at Nine O'Clock

  1. Royal Maternity Hospital, 79 Lauriston Place: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB44033 (MacGibbon and Ross, 1879; Married Women's Pavilion 1895).
  2. Staff, numbers and practice, 1907: Royal Maternity Hospital Annual Report, 1907; Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08; Nuttall (2007). J. W. Ballantyne's campaign for antenatal care, including the "pre-maternity" bed endowed at the hospital in 1901: Lothian Health Services Archive.
  3. Infant mortality in Scotland, 1907: Registrar General for Scotland, annual report (about 118 deaths under one year per 1,000 births). Infant smallpox vaccination was compulsory in Scotland under the Vaccination (Scotland) Act 1863. Typhoid, cholera, plague and rabies vaccines existed by 1907 but were not given to infants; diphtheria could be treated with antitoxin, but no diphtheria immunization was in general use.

  1. Weather, July 4, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (8 a.m. 50°F, ENE force 3, overcast; maximum 56°F, minimum 47°F; 1.4 hours of sunshine; 0.01 in rain).

  1. Agnes Brown's occupation, domestic servant, and her domicile, Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar: her son's birth entry, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, registered July 4, 1907 (original image). No record found names her employer.

Deaths of Jane Henderson, June 8, 1891: Quothquan monumental inscriptions.

Petition for naturalization 139903, U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania, Pittsburgh, dated February 11, 1943: residence 612 California Avenue, Avalon; display manager, Bond Stores; description; last foreign residence Ayr; emigrated from Glasgow; arrival Detroit September 15, 1929, as Lawrence Brown; wife Constance Darcy, married Birmingham October 9, 1939; two daughters, both residing with him (original image). February 11, 1943 is the date of the petition; the San Francisco depositions followed on March 3 and the oath and admission on May 6, 1943. The 1929 passenger list and border card give Dunfermline as his last residence and Greenock as his port of embarkation (original images).
  2. Witnesses David Hunter, machinist, and Frank Holliday, clerk, knew him from September 1941: petition 139903 (original image; witnesses' addresses read provisionally).
  3. 612 California Avenue, Avalon (two-story brick, c. 1900, office with apartments over): Allegheny County assessment.
  4. Depositions of William Howard Vahlkamp and Betty Johnstone Sherwood, San Francisco, March 3, 1943 (original image).
  5. Oath of allegiance and order granting petition 139903 and admitting him to citizenship, May 6, 1943: oath and admission page of the petition (original image).
  6. Albert Blake Darcy's registration, Local Board Kent 2, Warwick, April 27, 1942 (original image).
  7. Final surrender of German forces at Stalingrad, February 2, 1943; Axis surrender in Tunisia, May 13, 1943: standard histories.
  8. The courtroom scene is described as it would have been. The oath is quoted in the general form used in 1943; the wording on his own oath page names the King of Great Britain.

Chapter 29: River Avenue

  1. Obituary, Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3: work for Pawtucket firms during the previous fifteen years (original image).
  2. Pawtucket city directory, 1947, p. 154: 97 Magill Street, wife Constance E., window dresser (original image).
  3. Providence city directory, 1950, p. 214: Lawrence B. (Constance), 148 General Street (original image); 1951, 1953, 1955: display worker, 148 General Street (index and transcription entries).
  4. Magill Street housing (e.g. no. 79, three-family, 1920): Pawtucket assessor; downtown Pawtucket stores: Downtown Pawtucket Historic District nomination.
  5. Hurricane Carol damage totals for New England (homes, automobiles, boats destroyed): U.S. Weather Bureau figures as reported in National Weather Service summaries of the storm.
  6. Death of Margaret Jane Darcy, September 10, 1942, 60 Blake Street, Shawomet, Warwick; informant her son Albert B. Darcy of the same address: death certificate 159 (original image).
  7. Albert Norman Darcy, d. October 1, 1954, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5, lot 84: Catholic cemetery-office index.
  8. Albert Blake Darcy, d. November 4, 1957, Mount Saint Mary Cemetery, Pawtucket, section 9, lot 278: cemetery-office index; grave marker.
  9. Naturalization oaths: Thomas Crombie, petition 327632, September 9, 1947; Janet Crombie, petition 329111, March 16, 1948 (original images).
  10. Providence city directories 1956, 1959: Laurence B. and Constance E., 644 River Avenue, display work (directory index entries).
  11. Providence city directory, 1960, p. 287: displayman, Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket, home 644 River (original image).
  12. Providence city directory, 1961, p. 259: window displays at 644 River Avenue; Constance E., nurse, Roger Williams General Hospital (original image).
  13. Constance Eugenie Darcy Douglas's nursing training: Rhode Island School of Practical Nursing, per her obituary.
  14. Laurence's dress and love of reading: family recollection, as told to the author.
  15. Scenes of family life are described as they would have been.

Chapter 30: The Ninth of March

  1. Lung cancer; the family's not knowing of it until he was hospitalized; his sudden admission: recollection of the author's mother. His death certificate, which would give the certified cause, has not been obtained. His dress, his love of reading and his nickname "Doug": family recollection.
  2. Death, Thursday, March 9, 1961, St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, after a brief illness; home 644 River Avenue; age 53; born Edinburgh, Scotland; late parents Robert and Elizabeth (Anderson) Douglas; Bond Clothing Co., own display business, fifteen years for Pawtucket firms; survivors as quoted: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image).
  3. Age at death calculated from the Edinburgh birth entry (June 14, 1907).
  4. St. Joseph's Hospital, 21 Peace Street: dedicated March 20, 1892, and opened in April 1892 as St. Joseph's Hospital for Incurables in the former Harris mansion; cornerstone of a new building laid July 2, 1893; west wing completed October 8, 1930; expansion 1954; Harris mansion razed March 1962: hospital and diocesan histories (secondary).
  5. 56 Dartmouth Avenue and 21 Peace Street lie on the same assessor's plat (44): Providence tax roll.
  6. The Mason Building, 165–169 Weybosset Street (1903); the Outlet Company across the street at 168–176 Weybosset: Downtown Providence historic-district and preservation records. Laurence's workplace at 165 Weybosset: Providence city directories, 1937 and 1938.
  7. Funeral announced for 10 a.m., Monday, March 13, 1961, Ruth E. Urquhart, 812 Greenwich Avenue, Warwick: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). This is an advance announcement; no separate record of the service itself has been seen.
  8. Burial, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5, lot 84: Laurence's own interment record has not been seen. The burial rests on the gravestone, known from a photograph in an Ancestry member gallery (inscriptions: Laurence B. Douglas 1907–1961; Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994), and on the Catholic cemeteries' index, which places Albert Norman Darcy (died October 1, 1954) and Constance Darcy Douglas (1994, grave 3) in section 5, lot 84.
  9. The hospital scenes and the burial are described as they would have been; the family recollection is that the illness was not known until he was admitted. Funeral and burial details follow the obituary and the gravestone.

Epilogue: The Names He Carried

  1. Warwick city directory 1963: Constance, widow of Lawrence B., nurse, 119 Phillips Avenue (original image). Warwick city directory 1965: 1292 Post Road, nurse, Briarcliffe Health Center, Johnston (text finding; page image not checked).
  2. Constance Darcy Douglas's practical-nurse training, eight years at Cranston General Hospital, retirement in 1974, residence on Sixth Street, East Greenwich, and St. Francis de Sales Church; death at Rhode Island Hospital; three daughters; the original newspaper page has not been seen. Her pleasant nature and the name "Nan": family recollection.
  3. Eugenie E. DeLaire Darcy, 1894–1966, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5: Find a Grave memorial 149385784 (secondary).
  4. Death of Constance Darcy Douglas, April 12, 1994; burial Saint Ann Cemetery, section 5, lot 84, grave 3: Catholic cemeteries' burial index. Stone inscription Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994: member-gallery photograph of the gravestone.
  5. Janet Crombie, b. April 29, 1900, d. December 1979, last residence Maywood, Illinois: Social Security Death Index, record 13228117 (index). Duchess of Bedford manifest, arrived September 13, 1929: see Chapter 20. Marriage record giving 1860 South Hamlin Avenue, Chicago: see Chapter 25.
  6. Betty Crombie Mitchell, d. June 23, 2009, Minneapolis: Minnesota Death Index; Star Tribune, June 25, 2009 (index). Jessie Crombie, d. December 12, 2015, Poplar Grove, Illinois: U.S. Obituary Collection, Janesville Gazette, December 15, 2015 (index).
  7. Marriage of Agnes McGarth Brown and Thomas McKenzie, 1911 (original register image). Daughters Mary and Jean: Thomas McKenzie's First World War army service papers (original image). Agnes's portrait: Ancestry member galleries; the provenance description is the sharer's, not independently verified.
  8. Laurence in Pennsylvania from about September 1941: his naturalization witnesses' acquaintance with him from that month (petition 139903, original image) and family knowledge. Where each spouse was on December 7, 1941, is not separately documented.
  9. The pocket watch and the word "Edinburgh" inside its case: in the author's possession.
  10. Elizabeth Anderson's later life and date of death are not known; the obituary of 1961 calls her "the late." Whether Agnes knew what became of her son is not known.

The records cited note by note in the Sources, together with the archival collections, directories, newspapers and published works consulted in reconstructing the life of Laurence Brown Douglas and the world he moved through.

Civil registration, census and vital records

National Records of Scotland, Statutory Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths (ScotlandsPeople), including St Giles, Edinburgh, births 1907 (685/04 0839) and marriages 1911 (685/04 0616); Peebles births 1885 (768/00 0149).

Census of Scotland, 1851, 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901, 1911 and 1921; Census of England and Wales, 1881 and 1901; Census of the British Army overseas, 1911.

Old Parish Registers and Catholic Parish Registers of Scotland (ScotlandsPeople).

Registrar General for Scotland, Annual Reports and Detailed Annual Reports, 1900–1925.

U.S. Federal Census, 1900–1950; Rhode Island State Census, 1925 and 1936.

Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Illinois and Alabama birth, marriage and death records; Cook County, Illinois, Marriage Index; Jefferson County, Alabama, Marriage License Records, 1939.

Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, and Mount Saint Mary Cemetery, Pawtucket, interment records.

Immigration, emigration and naturalization

UK Outward and Incoming Passenger Lists (The National Archives, BT 27 and BT 26), 1890–1960.

Canadian Passenger Lists, 1865–1935 (Library and Archives Canada, RG 76-C); Form 30A Ocean Arrivals.

U.S. Border Crossings from Canada to the United States, Detroit, Port Huron and Blaine, 1895–1956.

New York Passenger and Crew Lists, 1938 (NARA T715).

Naturalization records, U.S. District Court, Western District of Pennsylvania (petition 139903, 1943); Chicago naturalization petitions 327632 and 329111; Declarations of Intention and Petitions for Naturalization, NARA.

Alien Registration Forms (AR-2) and Alien Case Files (A-Files), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and the National Archives and Records Administration.

Thomas E. Appleton, Ravenscrag: The Allan Royal Mail Line (Toronto: McClelland and Stewart, 1974).

Marjory Harper, Emigration from Scotland Between the Wars: Opportunity or Exile? (Manchester University Press, 1998); Scotland No More? The Scots Who Left Scotland in the Twentieth Century (Luath Press, 2012).

Military service records

British Army First World War service records and medal index cards (The National Archives, WO 363 and WO 372).

Soldiers Died in the Great War, 1914–1919.

Commonwealth War Graves Commission records.

Directories, gazetteers and maps

Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1900–1920; Post Office Dunfermline Directory.

The County Directory of Scotland (Edinburgh: R. & R. Clark), editions of 1862–1912.

Macdonald’s Scottish Directory and Gazetteer (Edinburgh), various years.

Slater’s Royal National Commercial Directory of Scotland.

City directories of Providence, Pawtucket and Warwick, Rhode Island; Chicago; and San Francisco, 1913–1965.

Ordnance Survey of Scotland, six-inch and twenty-five-inch county series, Lanarkshire, Midlothian and Fife; National Library of Scotland digitized maps.

Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps of Providence, Pawtucket and Chicago.

Bradshaw’s Railway Guide, May 1900.

Newspapers and periodicals

The Scotsman; Edinburgh Evening News; Dunfermline Press; Dunfermline Journal.

Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961; Providence Journal and Evening Bulletin.

Birmingham Post and Birmingham Age-Herald, October 10, 1939.

San Francisco Chronicle, December 1941, and “SF at war: a time of air raids, blackouts and joining the effort,” 2016.

The Northwestern Miller, Minneapolis, 1904.

Board of Trade, Labour Gazette, 1906.

Edinburgh and the Lothians

James Grant, Cassell’s Old and New Edinburgh, 3 vols. (London, 1880–1883).

Royal Maternity Hospital, Edinburgh, Annual Report, 1907.

Lothian Health Services Archive, Edinburgh University Library: Royal Maternity Hospital records (LHB3) and Lauriston Home papers (GD1/7).

A. Nuttall, “‘Because of poverty brought into hospital’,” Social History of Medicine 20, no. 2 (2007): 263–280.

Lauriston Home and Edinburgh poor-law and parish records.

Dunfermline, Fife and Andrew Carnegie

Ebenezer Henderson, The Annals of Dunfermline and Vicinity (Glasgow: John Tweed, 1879).

Andrew Carnegie, Autobiography of Andrew Carnegie (Boston: Houghton Mifflin, 1920).

Queen Anne School admission registers, Dunfermline.

Records of the Rosyth Royal Dockyard and the building of the naval base on the Forth.

Quothquan, Thankerton and Libberton community and parish local-history records.

Scottish Indexes, Lanark Sheriff Court paternity index.

The London Gazette, 1907 and 1914–1919.

Chicago

Cook County Assessor; Chicago ward and precinct records.

The 1938 New England Hurricane

American Experience, “The Hurricane of ’38,” PBS/WGBH; National Weather Service, Boston, “The Great New England Hurricane of 1938.”

San Francisco and the wartime home front

San Francisco Assessor records, 1940–1941.

Contemporary reporting on the December 1941 West Coast air-raid alarms and blackouts.

Weather and climate data

Met Office, Daily Weather Report, 1906–1930.

National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, Global Historical Climatology Network daily records.

Environment and Climate Change Canada, historical daily climate data.

George F. Black, The Surnames of Scotland: Their Origin, Meaning, and History (New York Public Library, 1946).

D. J. Steel, Sources for Scottish Genealogy and Family History, National Index of Parish Registers, vol. 12 (London: Society of Genealogists, 1970).

Probate Calendar of England and Wales, 1937–1966.

Ancestry, ScotlandsPeople, FamilySearch and FindMyPast online indexes and record images, as cited note by note.

Family photographs and the pocket watch of Laurence Brown Douglas, in the author’s possession.
